My Colts vs Texans prediction for Thursday Night Football starts with a Houston team that has lost all four of its games at Reliant Stadium in the franchise's 25th season. The pick against the spread is Colts +12.5, my over/under pick is Over 44.5, and the score I'll defend is Texans 26, Colts 20.

Houston threw itself a 25th anniversary party on October 4, with Liberty White jerseys, Battle Red socks, Andre Johnson and Arian Foster at halftime, and the Cowboys on the schedule just like the first game back in 2002. Dallas won 34-30. Buffalo, Cincinnati and the Giants have also left Reliant happy. The Texans' three wins came at Tennessee, in London against Jacksonville and 44-22 at the Chargers. A team that hasn't won at home has no business laying 12.5 to anybody on a short week.

The Formula: Net ratings Houston Texans −2.5, Indianapolis Colts −8.7 (nflverse play-by-play, Nov 17, 2026).

Houston is the better team Thursday, and nobody in Indianapolis is arguing otherwise. Lou Ferraro will remind you the Colts already beat this team 19-17 in Week 3, and he's right. Indianapolis is 3-7 with a 1-4 road record, and Daniel Jones has 12 interceptions, so nobody is selling this roster as pretty. But Jonathan Taylor has 739 yards and eight rushing touchdowns, and a steady run game is how a big underdog keeps a game inside two scores when both teams are on four days of rest and the Colts have to fly 871 miles.

Nate Coleman counters with C.J. Stroud's 19 touchdown throws against three interceptions, with Nico Collins and with Will Anderson Jr.'s 10.5 sacks. That's why Houston wins. It isn't why Houston wins by two touchdowns. The money went the other way anyway: the Action Network consensus opened at Houston −11.5 early Tuesday and sits at −12.5 now.

The room is lopsided. Four cards take Indianapolis with the points: The Formula at Texans 28, Colts 21, Next Man Up at Texans 26, Colts 22, Letdown Watch at Texans 27, Colts 19, and In The Trenches at Texans 24, Colts 19. Follow The Money is the only card laying the 12.5, riding that one-point move. On the total, The Formula, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch are on the Over 44.5, In The Trenches is on the Under, and Follow The Money has no total pick.

The Over comes from how much both defenses have given up. Houston has scored 233 and allowed 219 in nine games, and Indianapolis has scored 208 and allowed 271 in ten. Texans 26, Colts 20 adds up to 46, a point and a half clear of the total, and a six-point Houston win leaves the Colts with six and a half points to spare.

Nate finally gets his home win in the anniversary season. Lou keeps the laminated Week 3 box score in his pocket, and it still means something on the ride home.

display.fanatic_story:
Indianapolis Colts vs Houston Texans on Thursday night in Week 11 lands in a building that threw the Texans a 25th birthday party and still hasn't handed them a win. Nate Coleman was at Reliant Stadium on October 4 when the old Liberty White jerseys came back out, Andre Johnson and Arian Foster waved at halftime and Dallas walked off with a 34-30 win, and Lou Ferraro has texted him that date every morning since.

Lou drove down from Indianapolis on Wednesday with a cooler of sandwiches and a printed copy of the Week 3 box score. It says Colts 19, Texans 17. He had it laminated.

Nate: You laminated a September game.

Lou: I laminate everything that goes right for us. It's a short stack.

He isn't wrong about the stack. Indianapolis is 3-7. The Colts lost four straight before Sunday, including a 42-7 day in Jacksonville that Lou refers to only as the weather event. Then they beat Miami 24-22 at Lucas Oil, and Lou walked out of that building like somebody had handed him the deed.

Nate's problem is a strange one. His team is 3-6, and all three wins came somewhere else: Tennessee, London, and a 44-22 beating of the Chargers in Los Angeles. At home it's four games and four losses, to Buffalo, Cincinnati, Dallas and the Giants. The Texans have been better tourists than hosts all year, and in a 25th season that was sold as a homecoming, that hurts.

Nate: We wore the Battle Red socks for Dallas. They invited back Billy Miller, the guy who scored the first touchdown this franchise ever had. And we lost.

Lou: Maybe stop inviting people.

What Nate does have is C.J. Stroud, and he'll talk about him until you physically leave. Stroud has 19 touchdown throws and only three interceptions. Nico Collins is the target Nate trusts on third down, and Will Anderson Jr. has 10.5 sacks, a figure Nate keeps on a sticky note on the dashboard right next to his toll tag.

Lou answers with one name. Jonathan Taylor has 739 rushing yards and eight touchdowns, and Lou's entire plan for Thursday is to hand Taylor the ball until the crowd gets quiet enough to hear the air conditioning. He doesn't enjoy talking about Daniel Jones and his 12 interceptions, so he simply doesn't.

Both teams are on four days of rest. Houston lost 27-24 in Cleveland on Sunday, the Colts squeezed past Miami by two, and nobody's legs will be fresh by the fourth quarter.

Lou: You know what I like about a Thursday game? Nobody has time to fix anything. You are what you are.

Nate: We're 0-4 at home. That's what we are.

He says it, then hears it, and hates every word.

Nate does have a theory, the kind only a man who has sat in the same section since 2002 is allowed to have. His Texans have looked loosest on the road, where nobody expected anything and Stroud could just throw. At home, with the anniversary banners and the legends and the H-Town chant, they've pressed. Thursday is just a Thursday. No ceremony, no commemorative ticket, no halftime tribute. Only the Colts.

Nate: No more birthday parties. Just football.

Lou: That's the saddest thing I've ever heard a man say about his own stadium.

Lou will sit in the visitors' corner in a horseshoe cap and hold up the laminated box score after every Taylor first down. Nate will be in his usual seat with his Battle Red socks pulled up to his knees, waiting on luck that hasn't shown up yet. For once he thinks it's his turn.

My call: Texans 26, Colts 20.

The new $2.1 billion building in Orchard Park opened on June 23, and the Bills christened it with a 41-31 win over Detroit on a Thursday night in September. They're 3-1 there, with the only miss a 29-26 loss to New England, and 5-0 on the road. Ellen Marsh will tell you this is the best Bills team she's ever watched, and at 8-1 with 287 points scored, she's earned the right to say it.

The Formula: Net ratings Buffalo Bills 2.8, Miami Dolphins −9.3 (nflverse play-by-play, Nov 17, 2026).

Miami's only win came at the Jets, and its last game was a two-point loss in Indianapolis with Kyle McCord starting after Malik Willis went on injured reserve. That's a team losing close, not a team getting blown out every week.

Carla Ruiz has one tool she trusts, and it's the run game. Ollie Gordon II has 539 yards and four rushing touchdowns, and a Miami team that runs the ball shortens the game. That's how a 16.5-point spread survives, even against James Cook III and his 971 rushing yards and nine touchdowns.

The room agrees on the side, with one card sitting out. Carla will freeze, and the Bills will win. Neither of those things requires Buffalo to win by 17.

Ellen Marsh has a new seat, a new concourse to get lost in and a new parking routine, and on Sunday she finally gets to show all of it to the one Dolphins fan she'd happily drive through a snow squall to annoy. Carla Ruiz flies up from Miami for Miami Dolphins vs Buffalo Bills in Week 11, her first look at the new $2.1 billion Highmark Stadium in Orchard Park, and Ellen has promised her the full tour, slowly.

The building officially opened on June 23. Sixty thousand seats, 1.6 million square feet, the biggest construction job Western New York has ever seen, and not a roof in sight.

Carla: You spent two billion dollars and forgot the top.

Ellen: We didn't forget it. We declined it. Roofs are for people who are afraid of November.

Carla is from a city that considers anything below seventy a coat day, so she has packed like an arctic explorer. Ellen has packed a seat cushion, a thermos of cocoa and a list of grievances that she reads like scripture.

The list starts with the only home loss of the season, 29-26 to New England on October 4. Ellen does not discuss it. She refers to it as the incident. Everything else in the new place has gone right. The first regular-season game in the building was a Thursday night in September, a 41-31 win against Detroit, and Ellen was there two hours before the gates opened.

Buffalo is 8-1. The Bills are 5-0 on the road, which Ellen enjoys almost as much as winning at home, because it means somebody else's fans had to go home quiet. They won 31-12 at the Jets on Sunday.

Carla's season has been the opposite of all that. Miami is 1-8, with the only win coming at the Jets in October. Malik Willis is on injured reserve, and Kyle McCord started last week's 24-22 loss in Indianapolis. Carla liked parts of it. She liked the two points. She did not like the part where it was still a loss.

Carla: We were a field goal from 2-8. You know how close that is to respectable?

Ellen: That's not a sentence anyone has ever said out loud.

Carla's real hope is the ground game. Ollie Gordon II has 539 yards and four rushing touchdowns, and he runs like a guy who's personally offended by tacklers. Jordyn Brooks has 84 tackles and spends most Sundays chasing somebody else's mistakes. Chop Robinson has five sacks, and Carla wants every one of those numbers doubled by about four o'clock.

Ellen's answer is a list of names that sounds like a winter forecast. Josh Allen has 13 touchdown throws. James Cook III has 971 rushing yards and nine touchdowns, which Ellen will remind you is more yards than some entire backfields. Greg Rousseau has eight sacks. Dalton Kincaid has 487 receiving yards. She recites all of it in the voice of a woman reading a will.

Carla: You know you have more yards from one running back than some teams have from their quarterback?

display.fanatic_story:
One million lights come on along North Michigan Avenue on Saturday night, block by block, and Walt Brenner intends to be standing at Oak Street when the first tree goes. Andre Thibault, up from New Orleans for New Orleans Saints vs Chicago Bears in Week 11, has been told the 35th Magnificent Mile Lights Festival is the warmup act, and that Sunday at Soldier Field is the main event.

Andre comes from a city that knows parades. He has opinions about parades. He has stood on St. Charles Avenue since before he could walk, and he arrived in Chicago ready to grade this one on floats, bands and whether anybody throws anything.

Walt: Nobody throws anything. It's a lights parade. Mickey and Minnie lead it.

Andre: Then what do you catch?

Walt: A cold.

The parade steps off at 5:30 from Oak Street, nearly 40 floats heading south toward the river, with fireworks above the Chicago River after the last float passes. Walt has done it with his grandkids every year they've let him. He also uses it the way some fans use a pregame meal. He calls it loading up on good luck before the Bears need it.

They might not need much. Chicago is 7-2, rested off a bye and riding four straight wins, the last one a 27-24 win against Tampa Bay on a Sunday night. Caleb Williams has eight touchdown throws and five interceptions, and Walt will defend every one of those five like they were somebody else's fault. D'Andre Swift has 10 rushing touchdowns. Luther Burden III has 644 receiving yards, and Walt says he runs routes like a man late for the L.

Andre has his own list, and it's longer than his record would suggest. Tyler Shough has 2,173 yards and 15 touchdown throws. Chris Olave has 59 catches for 764 yards. Carl Granderson has 8.5 sacks and has spent the season living in other teams' backfields.

Walt: You're 3-6.

Andre: We're 2-1 on the road. We play better when nobody's feeding us.

That part is true, and it's the part Andre hangs on to hardest. The Saints won at Baltimore and at the Giants. They lost by a point in Detroit on opening day. It's the home games that have been a mess, and Sunday isn't a home game. His Saints lost 20-17 to Carolina last week, and he drove to the airport still muttering about it.

Then there's the forecast, and this is where Walt gets a look on his face. AccuWeather has gusts up to 31 miles an hour at Soldier Field around kickoff with the temperature near 49. Andre has played in a dome for as long as he's been alive. Walt has lived on the lakefront for most of his.

Walt: You ever thrown a football into a 31-mile-an-hour wind?

Andre: I've never thrown a football into any wind. We have a roof. We have air conditioning. We have civilization.

Walt: You have a roof because you're scared of the weather.

Andre: We have a roof because it rains sideways eight months a year.

They both have a point, which neither will admit. Wind like that does strange things to kicks, to deep shots, to a quarterback's patience. Walt thinks it helps a team built on the ground, and Chicago's defense has allowed only 184 points in nine games. Andre thinks the wind is the great equalizer and that Shough's quick throws can cut right through it.

Saturday night they'll stand together on Michigan Avenue, Walt in his old navy parka and Andre in three borrowed layers, watching the trees light up one after another. Sunday afternoon they'll be on opposite sides of a cold, loud building by the lake, and one of them will be very glad he came.

My call: Bears 28, Saints 20.

Rally Day brings DeMarcus Ware back to AT&T Stadium on Saturday, and my Titans vs Cowboys prediction says the Dallas defense will need all the nostalgia it can get. Tennessee +8 is the pick on the spread, the over/under call is Under 54.5, and Cowboys 28, Titans 23 is how I see it ending.

Cole Garrison spent Saturday walking Pete Varga through the stadium tour and the free health screenings, mostly so somebody could check his blood pressure before kickoff. A week after San Francisco put up 46 in a 46-40 loss, nobody in Arlington feels great about laying points with this defense.

The Formula: Net ratings Dallas Cowboys −6.4, Tennessee Titans −10.3 (nflverse play-by-play, Nov 17, 2026).

Dallas is the better team, and that's not the argument. The argument is whether a team that's 1-4 at home and has allowed 282 points in ten games should be giving eight to anybody. Tennessee is 1-8 and lost 40-23 to Jacksonville on Sunday, so Pete isn't selling a contender. He's selling a team with Cam Ward throwing and Tony Pollard running for six touchdowns, which is enough to hang around against a defense that just gave up 46.

The room tilts toward Tennessee. The Formula has Cowboys 28, Titans 23, Next Man Up has Cowboys 28, Titans 24, and In The Trenches has Cowboys 29, Titans 24. All three take Tennessee with the points. Letdown Watch is the only card laying the 8, at Cowboys 28, Titans 19. Follow The Money has no side pick and no total pick, with neither the spread nor the total moving off 8 and 54.5. Every card with a score is on the Under 54.5.

The Under is where this gets interesting, because Dallas games have been wild. The Cowboys have scored 286 and allowed 282. But the other half of this matchup is a Titans offense that has scored 167 all season, and that's what makes 54.5 too high. Tennessee isn't built to trade touchdowns for four quarters, and Ward has eight touchdown throws in nine games.

Dak Prescott will get his. He has 21 touchdown throws, and CeeDee Lamb has 976 receiving yards. Dallas puts up 28 and the defense gives back 23, which is about what this team does on an ordinary Sunday. Cowboys 28, Titans 23 adds up to 51, three and a half under the total, and a five-point Dallas win leaves Tennessee three points to spare.

For a Cowboys team heading into a holiday game on a short week, a five-point win would feel like relief. It wouldn't feel like eight.

Cowboys 28, Titans 23. Titans cover the 8. Under 54.5.

display.fanatic_story:
DeMarcus Ware will be shaking hands at AT&T Stadium on Saturday, and Cole Garrison has already decided that's the closest thing to a fourth-down stop the Cowboys will see all weekend. Pete Varga drove down from Nashville for Tennessee Titans vs Dallas Cowboys in Week 11 and got dragged straight to Rally Day, the open house the Cowboys throw in Arlington the day before every home game.

It runs 10 to 5 with free parking, stadium tours and free health screenings for anyone who registers. Cole signed them both up.

Pete: You drove me to a football stadium to get my blood pressure checked.

Cole: I drove you here so somebody could take it before Sunday. After Sunday, it's going to be a medical event.

Pete laughed, because he's 1-8 and laughing is about all a Titans fan has left in November. Tennessee hasn't won a home game all season. Its only win came in Indianapolis in October, 26-20, and Pete has the radio call saved on his phone the way other people save wedding videos. Last Sunday was a 40-23 loss to Jacksonville at home, and he left early, which he has never done in his life.

What keeps him coming back is the kid. Cam Ward has 1,714 yards and eight touchdown throws in a season where the protection has been a rumor. Tony Pollard has 628 yards and six touchdowns. Jacob Martin has 7.5 sacks, and Anthony Hill Jr. has 82 tackles, most of them earned the hard way.

Cole doesn't argue. He can't, not after the week he's had.

Dallas lost 46-40 to San Francisco on Sunday. Forty-six. At home. Cole was there, and he says it felt like watching your house get robbed while you held the door. The Cowboys are 4-6 and 1-4 at AT&T Stadium, and the only home win came in September against Washington.

Cole: We score. Nobody's ever said we don't score.

That much is true. Dak Prescott has 2,724 yards and 21 touchdown throws against six interceptions. CeeDee Lamb has 77 catches for 976 yards and eight touchdowns, and Cole talks about him like he's describing a sunset. Javonte Williams has nine rushing touchdowns. Dallas has put up 286 points in ten games.

It's the other 282 that keep Cole up at night.

Pete: You've given up 282 points.

Cole: I know what we've given up. Don't read me my own mail.

So the tour, for Cole, had a purpose. He narrated it like a museum guide for better defenses, then went quiet near the field like a man at a memorial. Ware was the headliner on Saturday for a reason. Cole has a Ware jersey he still wears to Thanksgiving, and he reminds anyone who'll listen that the Cowboys have their own holiday game coming in a few days and would like to arrive at it in a better mood.

Pete's hopes are simple. He wants Ward to have time. He wants Pollard to get 20 carries. He wants Dallas to keep giving up points the way it has, because the Titans have scored only 167 all year and need all the help they can get.

Cole's hopes are simpler. Stop somebody. Anybody. Quinnen Williams has six sacks and safety Caleb Downs has 66 tackles, and Cole says those two are the reason he still bothers to stay through the fourth quarter.

They'll go to the game together on Sunday, Pete in navy and light blue, Cole in a Ware jersey that hasn't fit right in years. Somewhere in the second half, Pete will start to think the Titans might hang around. Cole will start to think about the holiday.

My call: Cowboys 28, Titans 23.

Detroit lost Aidan Hutchinson for the season to a torn ACL during a sack celebration in Munich, and my Buccaneers vs Lions prediction starts there. Tampa Bay +6.5 gets my spread pick and Over 45.5 gets my over/under pick, with Lions 26, Buccaneers 22 as the final.

Martin Sorensen took the news the way Detroit takes most November news, by going skating. The Rink at Campus Martius Park opens Saturday with an Ugly Holiday Sweater Party under the city's Christmas tree, and Sal Ferris, in from Tampa, has been handed a pirate-ship sweater for the occasion.

The Formula: Net ratings Detroit Lions −0.4, Tampa Bay Buccaneers −5.2 (nflverse play-by-play, Nov 17, 2026).

Dan Campbell confirmed the injury on Tuesday and called it a gut punch, and he wasn't exaggerating. Hutchinson has six sacks this season and 49 since Detroit drafted him in 2022. The Lions are still 7-2 and 4-0 at Ford Field, and nobody here is saying they lose. But 6.5 is a lot to lay with the defensive front suddenly missing its best player, against a Tampa Bay team that has scored 202 points and allowed 178. That's a better point differential than a 3-6 record suggests, and the Bucs are rested, coming off a bye after a 27-24 loss in Chicago.

Tampa Bay has three cards in its corner. Next Man Up has Lions 25, Buccaneers 23, Letdown Watch has Lions 27, Buccaneers 22, and In The Trenches has Lions 23, Buccaneers 21. The Formula is the one card laying the 6.5, at Lions 27, Buccaneers 20. Follow The Money sits this one out, because the spread has held at 6.5 and the total at 45.5 since early Tuesday. The Formula, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch all take the Over, and In The Trenches takes the Under.

The Over comes from Detroit's offense. The Lions have scored 257 points in nine games, Jared Goff has 18 touchdown throws, Jahmyr Gibbs has 1,000 rushing yards and 11 touchdowns, and Amon-Ra St. Brown has 755 receiving yards. Bucky Irving brings 825 rushing yards of his own for Tampa Bay. Lions 26, Buccaneers 22 is 48 points, enough to clear 45.5, and Detroit by four stays inside the spread.

Without Hutchinson, Detroit is still good enough to win. It just isn't the same team up front, and against a rested opponent that matters.

Lions 26, Buccaneers 22. Buccaneers cover the 6.5. Over 45.5.

display.fanatic_story:
Martin: Don't say his name in the car.

Sal Ferris had not said Aidan Hutchinson's name in the car. He had said "tough break" once, somewhere around Toledo on I-75, and Martin Sorensen turned the radio up. That was the whole conversation for forty miles.

So Martin will tell it once, for Tampa Bay Buccaneers vs Detroit Lions in Week 11, and then he'd like everyone to stop asking. Hutchinson sacked Drake Maye in the first quarter in Munich, celebrated, and tore the ACL in his right knee. He's done for the season. Dan Campbell confirmed it Tuesday on 97.1 The Ticket and called it a gut punch. Hutchinson is 26, he has six sacks this year and 49 since Detroit took him second in 2022, and Martin has his jersey hanging in the hallway like a family portrait.

The Lions won that game 35-10. Nobody in Detroit remembers the score.

Sal: You're still 7-2.

Martin: I know we're 7-2. I also know who isn't going to be chasing quarterbacks for the next two months.

So Martin did what Detroit does in late November when the news is bad. He went skating. The Rink at Campus Martius Park opens Saturday with the Ugly Holiday Sweater Party, six to eleven at night, and you skate in circles beneath the city's Christmas tree. Martin owns a sweater with a lion in a Santa hat stitched across the front. He bought Sal one with a pirate ship on it, which Sal calls the nicest thing anyone has done for him all season.

It has been that kind of season in Tampa. The Bucs lost their first four, three of them at home, and Sal spent September apologizing to people at work. Then they won in Dallas, crushed Carolina 43-13 and shut out Atlanta 16-0, which Sal will bring up at every family dinner for the rest of his life. They've scored 202 points and allowed 178, which is not what a 3-6 team usually looks like.

The bye came after a 27-24 loss in Chicago that Sal still can't discuss. He spent the week off watching Bucky Irving highlights. Irving has 825 yards and seven touchdowns, and Sal calls him the most fun player in the division. Josiah Trotter has 76 tackles, and David Walker has four sacks.

Martin listens politely, then talks about Jahmyr Gibbs, which is what Martin does instead of sleeping. Gibbs has 1,000 rushing yards and 11 touchdowns. Jared Goff has 2,437 yards and 18 touchdown throws against four interceptions. Amon-Ra St. Brown has 65 catches for 755 yards. The Lions have scored 257 points in nine games, and Ford Field hasn't seen them lose yet.

Sal: So the offense is fine.

Martin: The offense was never the problem. The problem is that the guy who made the other quarterback nervous is gone until next year.

Alim McNeill has 6.5 sacks, and Jack Campbell has 57 tackles. Martin is counting on both of them a lot more this week than he was a week ago. He says the building will be loud enough to make up the rest. Sal points out that Ford Field has a roof, so at least the noise will have nowhere to go.

Saturday night they'll skate beneath the tree, two grown men in ugly sweaters, one of them trying very hard not to look at his phone for injury news. Sunday, Martin will wear the Hutchinson jersey anyway. Sal will wear the pirate sweater, mostly to annoy him, and for three hours Detroit will try to remember that 7-2 is still 7-2.

My call: Lions 26, Buccaneers 22.

display.fanatic_story:
The tree is on the wrong side.

That's the first thing Chet Morrell told Neil Carver at the airport, before hello and before the bags. Union Station's 30-foot Grand Hall tree is on the west side of the building this year, Holiday Reflections opens Friday, and Chet has feelings about it.

Neil: Is that good?

Chet: It's different. Kansas City doesn't love different in November.

Neil is in town for Arizona Cardinals vs Kansas City Chiefs in Week 11, and different is about the only thing he has going for him. The Cardinals are 3-7. They scored three points at Seattle and six at home against the Rams, a 34-6 loss that Neil watched from his couch with the sound off. He doesn't want to talk about quarterbacks. Arizona has used more than one this year, and he has stopped buying jerseys with names on the back.

What he will talk about is the road. Arizona is 0-4 at home and 3-3 away, and Neil has decided that's a personality trait. The Cardinals won at the Chargers in September, won 18-16 at the Rams in October and won a 33-30 shootout in Dallas on the first of November. Neil was in Arlington for that one. He still has the ticket stub in his wallet next to his driver's license.

Chet: So your plan is that your team is better on vacation.

Neil: My plan is Trey McBride.

McBride has 78 catches for 635 yards and five touchdowns, and Neil talks about him like a brother who went to law school. Tyler Allgeier has 383 rushing yards. Mack Wilson Sr. has 72 tackles, and Budda Baker, who Neil says has been the heartbeat of that defense for years, has 3.5 sacks. Mike LaFleur's team doesn't quit, and Neil wants that on the record.

Chet listens the way people in Kansas City listen to visitors in November, politely and with a little pity. The Chiefs are 7-2 and haven't lost at Arrowhead this season. They've allowed 156 points in nine games. They put up 35 on the Jets and then 35 more in Atlanta last Sunday, and Chet has been in a good mood for about two weeks.

Patrick Mahomes has 2,385 yards and 19 touchdown throws against four interceptions. Kenneth Walker III has 872 yards and seven touchdowns, and Chet has already started calling him by his first name. Travis Kelce has 512 receiving yards. Nick Bolton has 89 tackles, and George Karlaftis has 5.5 sacks.

Neil: What do you do the night before a game?

Chet: Union Station. Friday they light the place up, there's a streetcar the size of a parade float on Petticoat Lane, and the kids get a frozen wonderland with fake snow. I go stand by the tree.

Neil: The tree that switched sides.

Chet: I'll get used to it.

They'll go Friday night and take the same photo by the tree that Chet takes every year, except this year the background is wrong. Sunday the lots open four and a half hours before a noon kickoff, and Chet will be in his spot by 7:30 with the grill going. The forecast calls for 49 degrees and no rain, which Chet calls perfect and Neil, a man from Phoenix, considers a hardship.

Neil doesn't need the Cardinals to win. He'd like them to make it interesting into the fourth quarter, and he'd like McBride to have a big day. Chet would like the tree back on the east side of Grand Hall, but he'll settle for 8-2.

My call: Chiefs 28, Cardinals 18.

display.fanatic_story:
Somebody in Philadelphia put up a 65-foot Ferris wheel this week, and Ray Donnelly is just relieved that something in this city is going up.

The Christmas Village preview weekend opens Saturday at LOVE Park, City Hall's Courtyard and North Broad, and Ray has been planning his route like a parade marshal. Bratwurst first, then raclette, then the Churro Split, then one slow lap around the German Christmas pyramid, which is 30 feet tall and carries more than 3,000 lights. Ray has walked past it every year he can remember. This year he needs it more.

Ed Kowalski drove in from Pittsburgh for Pittsburgh Steelers vs Philadelphia Eagles in Week 11, and Ray met him at the Ferris wheel.

Ed: You look tired.

Ray: We've lost seven in a row, Ed. I look like a man who has lost seven in a row.

The Eagles started 2-0. Then came Chicago, the Rams, Jacksonville in London, Carolina, Dallas, Washington and the Giants, and Ray can name the worst moment of each one without being asked. Joe Milton III started the last one, a 19-11 home loss to the Giants, and the bye week since has been the quietest two weeks of Ray's football life. Philadelphia has scored 148 points in nine games, and the Eagles are 1-4 at the Linc.

So Ray is holding on to small things. Nolan Smith Jr. has five sacks. Zack Baun has 65 tackles and plays every snap like it insulted his family. Makai Lemon has 37 catches and keeps getting open. Saquon Barkley is still Saquon Barkley in Ray's head, whatever the season says.

Ed, to his credit, is not gloating. He just watched his team lose 38-18 in Cincinnati on Sunday night, and he hasn't fully recovered.

Ed: We were 6-2 going in. I was making plans.

Ray: What kind of plans?

Ed: The kind you don't say out loud in Pittsburgh.

The Steelers are 6-3 and 4-0 at home, but only 2-3 away. Aaron Rodgers has 2,014 yards and 15 touchdown throws against six interceptions. Jaylen Warren has 719 rushing yards. DK Metcalf has 432 receiving yards. T.J. Watt has 7.5 sacks, and Payton Wilson has 88 tackles, and Ed describes the two of them as the reason he still has hair. Mike McCarthy has already been asked about Cincinnati more times than Ed can stand.

They rode the Ferris wheel once. Ed held on with both hands. From the top you can see City Hall and the whole length of the holiday stalls, more than 120 vendors, and Ray pointed out every one he planned to eat at before Sunday.

Ed: You know they close this whole thing again on Monday.

Ray: For three days. Then it's back on Thanksgiving. Philadelphia always comes back, Ed.

Ed: Your team hasn't.

Ray let that one go. It was a fair shot.

The Linc will be loud for the first quarter no matter what, because it always is. Ray will bring the lucky scarf his late uncle gave him, and Ed has promised to keep his celebrating to a polite nod. What Ray wants is simple: one good afternoon, a defense that gets to Rodgers, and an end to the streak somewhere other than in his nightmares.

He'll probably have to wait another week. But it'll be close enough to keep him in his seat until the end.

My call: Steelers 22, Eagles 19.

Somebody in Philadelphia put up a 65-foot Ferris wheel this week, and Ray Donnelly is just relieved that something in this city is going up.

The Christmas Village preview weekend opens Saturday at LOVE Park, City Hall's Courtyard and North Broad, and Ray has been planning his route like a parade marshal. Bratwurst first, then raclette, then the Churro Split, then one slow lap around the German Christmas pyramid, which is 30 feet tall and carries more than 3,000 lights. Ray has walked past it every year he can remember. This year he needs it more.

Ed Kowalski drove in from Pittsburgh for Pittsburgh Steelers vs Philadelphia Eagles in Week 11, and Ray met him at the Ferris wheel.

Ed: You look tired.

Ray: We've lost seven in a row, Ed. I look like a man who has lost seven in a row.

The Eagles started 2-0. Then came Chicago, the Rams, Jacksonville in London, Carolina, Dallas, Washington and the Giants, and Ray can name the worst moment of each one without being asked. Joe Milton III started the last one, a 19-11 home loss to the Giants, and the bye week since has been the quietest two weeks of Ray's football life. Philadelphia has scored 148 points in nine games, and the Eagles are 1-4 at the Linc.

So Ray is holding on to small things. Nolan Smith Jr. has five sacks. Zack Baun has 65 tackles and plays every snap like it insulted his family. Makai Lemon has 37 catches and keeps getting open. Saquon Barkley is still Saquon Barkley in Ray's head, whatever the season says.

Ed, to his credit, is not gloating. He just watched his team lose 38-18 in Cincinnati on Sunday night, and he hasn't fully recovered.

Ed: We were 6-2 going in. I was making plans.

Ray: What kind of plans?

Ed: The kind you don't say out loud in Pittsburgh.

The Steelers are 6-3 and 4-0 at home, but only 2-3 away. Aaron Rodgers has 2,014 yards and 15 touchdown throws against six interceptions. Jaylen Warren has 719 rushing yards. DK Metcalf has 432 receiving yards. T.J. Watt has 7.5 sacks, and Payton Wilson has 88 tackles, and Ed describes the two of them as the reason he still has hair. Mike McCarthy has already been asked about Cincinnati more times than Ed can stand.

They rode the Ferris wheel once. Ed held on with both hands. From the top you can see City Hall and the whole length of the holiday stalls, more than 120 vendors, and Ray pointed out every one he planned to eat at before Sunday.

Ed: You know they close this whole thing again on Monday.

Ray: For three days. Then it's back on Thanksgiving. Philadelphia always comes back, Ed.

Ed: Your team hasn't.

Ray let that one go. It was a fair shot.

The Linc will be loud for the first quarter no matter what, because it always is. Ray will bring the lucky scarf his late uncle gave him, and Ed has promised to keep his celebrating to a polite nod. What Ray wants is simple: one good afternoon, a defense that gets to Rodgers, and an end to the streak somewhere other than in his nightmares.

He'll probably have to wait another week. But it'll be close enough to keep him in his seat until the end.

display.fanatic_story:
Mitch Kovac has a minivan, a thermos of hot chocolate and a ticket for one vehicle, which is how Speedway Christmas sells them. On Friday night he plans to drive Owen Pratt around Charlotte Motor Speedway in Concord, slowly, past the lights, and let the man decompress.

Owen needs it. He flew down from Baltimore for Baltimore Ravens vs Carolina Panthers in Week 11 carrying the face of a fan whose team has lost five straight.

Owen: Don't talk to me about Monday.

Mitch: I wasn't going to.

Mitch was absolutely going to. The Chargers came into Baltimore on Monday night without a win all season and left with a 23-20 victory, and Owen watched it from the couch with the lights off. Before that it was Cleveland, then Cincinnati, then Buffalo, then Jacksonville. After the Chargers loss, Kyle Hamilton said the Ravens are disgracing the team's standards. Owen has thought about that sentence every hour since.

Owen: He's right. That's the worst part. He's right.

Jacoby Brissett started Monday. Derrick Henry still has 699 yards and ten rushing touchdowns, and Owen talks about him like a lighthouse in a storm. Zay Flowers has 688 receiving yards. Roquan Smith has 82 tackles, and Mike Green has 5.5 sacks. The Ravens are 4-6 and 1-4 at home, but 3-2 on the road, including a 41-23 win in Indianapolis to open the season and a 34-31 shootout with Dallas in Rio.

Owen: We play better away from our own fans.

Mitch: That's a sad thing to say out loud.

Owen: It's been a sad season.

Mitch can't gloat, because Carolina is 4-5 and has its own scars. The Panthers gave up 59 to Chicago in the opener, at home, and Mitch still flinches when anybody says the word fifty. They lost 43-13 to Tampa Bay in October. But they beat Detroit 32-26, won in Philadelphia, and came out of New Orleans last week with a 20-17 win, and Mitch has been in a forgiving mood ever since.

Bryce Young has 2,397 yards and 16 touchdown throws against six interceptions. Chuba Hubbard has 711 yards and seven touchdowns. Tetairoa McMillan has 660 receiving yards, and Mitch says he's the first Panthers receiver in years who makes him stand up before the catch. Devin Lloyd has 63 tackles. Jaelan Phillips has 3.5 sacks.

Owen: You're 1-3 at home.

Mitch: I'm aware. I was there for all three.

On Friday they'll do the Speedway lap twice, because Owen will ask for a second one and Mitch will say yes. It's the 17th year of the event, and Mitch has gone to most of them. He likes the part where the track opens up in front of you and the whole infield glows. Owen likes that nobody in the next car can see his face.

On Sunday, Owen plans to leave his phone in his pocket all afternoon so he can't read whatever Hamilton says next. Mitch plans to spend the first quarter explaining to the people around them that his friend is going through something.

What Owen wants is one week where his team looks like itself. What Mitch wants is a home win in front of people who have been very patient. One of them is getting his wish, but whoever loses won't lose by much, and both of them know it.

My call: Panthers 24, Ravens 22.

display.fanatic_story:
At 5:30 on Friday evening, somebody on the Auraria Campus will flip a switch, and a 110-foot tree on the Tivoli Quad will light up the Denver sky. Ruth Calder will be standing close enough to feel the warmth from the bulbs, or at least she'll say she can.

Vic Moreno will be standing next to her in a Raiders hoodie, which in Denver in late November is either brave or foolish, and Vic hasn't decided which. He has made this trip enough times to know the walk up to the stadium is uphill both ways, at least in his telling.

Vic: It's a big tree.

Ruth: It's the Mile High Tree. Everything here is mile high. You'll get used to it.

Vic drove up from Las Vegas for Las Vegas Raiders vs Denver Broncos in Week 11, and Ruth has planned his entire weekend around reminding him how things are going. Friday is the tree, Saturday afternoon is Trans-Siberian Orchestra at Ball Arena, and Sunday is a Broncos team that hasn't lost since early October.

The Broncos are 7-2 and 4-0 at home. They lost in San Francisco in Week 4, and they've won five straight since, the last one 26-21 in Carolina before the bye. Ruth will tell you none of the wins has been pretty. She'll also tell you she doesn't care. Bo Nix has 1,730 yards and 11 touchdown throws against four interceptions. Jaylen Waddle has 337 receiving yards, and J.K. Dobbins has 324 on the ground. Alex Singleton has 107 tackles, and Zach Allen has 4.5 sacks, and Ruth describes the defense the way some people describe a good furnace.

Ruth: It's not exciting. It just works.

Vic has had an exciting season, which is a polite way to say a stressful one. The Raiders are 4-6. They won at the Chargers, in New Orleans and in a 38-33 shootout with the Jets, and they're 3-2 on the road. At home they're 1-4, and the last one was a 21-13 loss to Seattle that Vic left talking to himself.

Fernando Mendoza started that game, and Vic has a lot of hope riding on the kid. Brock Bowers has 50 catches for 676 yards and six touchdowns, and Vic calls him the best thing in Las Vegas that doesn't have a neon sign. Ashton Jeanty has 380 rushing yards. Maxx Crosby has five sacks and still plays like he's mad at the whole state of Colorado. Nakobe Dean has 107 tackles, the same as Singleton, which Vic brings up more than once.

Vic: Your linebacker and my linebacker are tied.

Ruth: My linebacker's team is 7-2.

Saturday, they'll go to the Trans-Siberian Orchestra show, the three o'clock one, because Ruth's family has gone for years and Vic was told it wasn't optional. There will be lasers. There will be a lot of electric guitar. Vic will pretend not to enjoy it and fail.

Sunday the forecast says 52 degrees and calm at kickoff, which counts as a gift in Denver in November. Ruth has her orange scarf. Vic has the hoodie and a jacket underneath it that he swears he isn't wearing.

Ruth wants a sixth straight win and a quiet afternoon. Vic wants Bowers to get loose, Crosby to get home and Mendoza to look like the future. Both of them think this will be closer than people outside Denver expect, which is the one thing they agreed on all weekend.

My call: Broncos 27, Raiders 19.

The first 25,000 people through the gates at MetLife Stadium on Sunday get a military knit beanie, and Leon Drobny intends to be one of the first through the gate. He has done the math on the parking lot. He has done the math on the tunnel. Leon has been a Giants fan long enough to know that free things go fast in New Jersey.

It's Salute to Service day, and Leon's father served, so this one matters to him more than most. He'll wear the beanie the whole game even if it's warm.

Ivy Corcoran thinks it might be. She flew up from Jacksonville for Jacksonville Jaguars vs New York Giants in Week 11 and checked the forecast on the plane: 60 degrees, light wind.

Ivy: That's not beanie weather.

Leon: It's beanie weather if they give you a beanie.

The Giants have had ten days to stew. They lost 24-21 to Washington on Thursday night, and Leon spent the long weekend replaying the fourth quarter in his head like a song he hates. Before that they won in Houston and in Philadelphia, and he was starting to say things out loud he usually keeps to himself. They're 5-3-1, with a tie in Washington back in October that Leon still describes as a loss with a better attitude.

J.J. McCarthy started the Thursday game. Cam Skattebo has 496 yards and four touchdowns and runs like every carry is personal. Malik Nabers has 58 catches for 692 yards, and Leon says he's the most fun Giants receiver since he was a kid. Arvell Reese has 81 tackles and 4.5 sacks, and Leon is already shopping for the jersey.

Ivy listens to all of it the way you listen to someone describe a vacation you've already taken.

Ivy: We've outscored people by 125.

Leon: I read it.

Ivy: Two hundred sixty-nine to 144.

Leon: I said I read it.

Jacksonville is 7-2. The Jaguars lost in Denver in September and to Houston at Wembley in October, and they've won every other game, most of them comfortably. They beat Indianapolis 42-7, won 33-10 in Baltimore and won 40-23 in Tennessee last Sunday. Trevor Lawrence has 2,284 yards and 21 touchdown throws against five interceptions, and Ivy says he finally looks like the guy the city was promised. Parker Washington has 645 receiving yards and six touchdowns. Bhayshul Tuten has 609 yards on the ground. Foyesade Oluokun has 68 tackles.

Leon: You've been on the road two weeks in a row.

Ivy: We like the road.

Leon: Nobody likes New Jersey.

That one got a laugh out of both of them, which is the way it usually goes with Leon and Ivy. They met years ago at a game in this same stadium and have been arguing about football since.

Sunday afternoon, they'll sit together in the upper level. Leon will wear his beanie and his Lawrence Taylor jersey. Ivy will keep her opinions to a respectful volume, at least during the Salute to Service moments. She has family who served too, and she'll stand for those with everybody else.

After that, it's football. Leon thinks the ten days of rest will matter. Ivy thinks the Jaguars are better than anyone the Giants have seen in a month. Both of them are probably right, and both of them know this one is going to be tighter than it looks on paper.

My call: Jaguars 25, Giants 20.

Erik Dahl has never seen the Vikings play in Mexico City, for the simple reason that the Vikings never have. Sunday night at Estadio Banorte, that changes, and Erik has been practicing his Spanish on the plane, mostly the words for "where is my seat" and "that was holding."

Nora Haskell has done this before. She was in the building in November 2022, back when it was still called Estadio Azteca, when the 49ers beat Arizona 38-10, and she has been telling Erik about it since the schedule came out.

Nora: The noise is different here. It comes from everywhere.

Erik: It comes from everywhere in Minneapolis too.

Nora: Not like this.

Minnesota Vikings vs San Francisco 49ers in Week 11 is the first Sunday night game ever played outside the United States, and the NFL's first game in Mexico in four years. Tickets in the general sale went in about an hour back in September. Erik got his through a cousin and doesn't want to talk about what he owes the cousin now.

There is no public parking at the stadium, so they'll take the Tren Ligero to the Estadio Azteca station like everybody else, and the gates open at 3:30 for a 7:20 local kickoff. Nora has planned the afternoon down to the taco stand. Erik has planned it down to the jersey.

These two teams have history, and Erik brought the receipts. The all-time series is 25-25-1. The Vikings have won the last two meetings. Nora would like it noted that the six postseason meetings have gone San Francisco's way five times.

Erik: Regular season is all that counts tonight.

Nora: You're the one who brought up history.

The Vikings are 7-2 and have won with defense all year. They've allowed 126 points in nine games, the fewest of anyone Nora can name off the top of her head, and Andrew Van Ginkel has 8.5 sacks. Blake Cashman has 76 tackles. Kirk Cousins started the 30-10 win in Green Bay last Sunday, and Erik says that game was the most relaxed he's felt in years. Aaron Jones Sr. has 521 rushing yards, and Justin Jefferson has 467 receiving yards, which Erik considers a personal insult to Jefferson and wants explained.

The 49ers are 8-1. They opened the season in Melbourne, so a long trip isn't new, and last week they outlasted Dallas 46-40 in a game Nora watched standing up. Brock Purdy has 2,369 yards and 20 touchdown throws against five interceptions. Christian McCaffrey has ten rushing touchdowns, and George Kittle has 557 receiving yards. Fred Warner has 88 tackles and, as far as Nora is concerned, has never had a bad day in his life.

Nora: You know we're technically the home team.

Erik: In Mexico.

Nora: Technically.

Neither team is really at home. Both of them flew a long way to get here, both are coming off road wins, and both fan bases will be outnumbered by locals who just want to see football on a Sunday night in their own city. Nora loves that. Erik is starting to.

After the game, they'll ride the train back toward the city center and argue the whole way. Erik will want to talk about the defense. Nora will want to talk about Purdy. Somewhere around the second stop, they'll both admit it was worth the trip.

My call: 49ers 24, Vikings 19.

Stevie Wonder plays Songs in the Key of Life at Capital One Arena on Monday night at 8, fifteen minutes before kickoff in Landover, and my Bengals vs Commanders prediction has Washington staying close enough to justify skipping the show. Commanders +6.5 is my spread pick and Under 52.5 my over/under call, with Bengals 27, Commanders 23 the final.

Claire Benton chose the game over the 50th anniversary concert, and Laura Kessel, in from Cincinnati, has not let her forget it.

The Formula: Net ratings Washington Commanders −3.9, Cincinnati Bengals 1.6 (nflverse play-by-play, Nov 17, 2026).

Cincinnati is 7-2, has won five straight, and just beat Pittsburgh 38-18 on Sunday night. Joe Burrow has 27 touchdown throws against six interceptions, and Ja'Marr Chase has 878 receiving yards. The Bengals have scored 278 points, so there's no mystery about why they're laying points on the road. But Washington has had eleven days of rest after a 24-21 win against the Giants, Cincinnati has eight, and the Commanders have been better at home than on the road, 2-2-1 as the home team and 1-3 away.

This is the rare game where every card agrees. The Formula has Bengals 27, Commanders 23, Next Man Up has the same score, Letdown Watch has Bengals 26, Commanders 22, and In The Trenches has Bengals 28, Commanders 24. All four take Washington with the points and the Under 52.5. Follow The Money has no side and no total, with the spread at 6.5 and the total at 52.5 since just after midnight Tuesday.

The Under starts with how high 52.5 sits. Washington has scored 196 points in nine games, and Jayden Daniels has thrown only ten touchdown passes, with Stefon Diggs catching six of them. Daniels also has 280 rushing yards, which keeps drives alive and the clock running. Cincinnati's defense has allowed 193, the kind of number that rarely comes with a track meet attached. The Bengals can score, but they've also won games 20-6 in Houston and 35-13 in Baltimore without needing a shootout. It'll be 48 degrees with some wind in Landover on Monday night, and that rarely helps an offense.

Bengals 27, Commanders 23 comes to 50, under 52.5, and a four-point Cincinnati win keeps Washington inside the 6.5. Claire will miss the concert for a loss, but not for a blowout, and in a 3-5-1 season she'll call that progress.

display.fanatic_story:
Claire Benton had two tickets for Monday night. One was for Stevie Wonder at Capital One Arena, Songs in the Key of Life in its entirety for the album's 50th anniversary, doors at seven, show at eight. The other was for the Commanders in Landover, kickoff at 8:15.

She can't be in both places. She has known this for weeks, and she has handled it the way any reasonable person would, by complaining about it to everyone she meets.

Laura Kessel: You picked football.

Claire: I picked football. Don't make me say it again.

Laura drove in from Cincinnati for Cincinnati Bengals vs Washington Commanders in Week 11, and she has been trying very hard not to be smug about it. It isn't going well. The Bengals are 7-2 and have won five straight, the last one a 38-18 win against Pittsburgh on Sunday night, and Laura has been smiling at strangers on the street.

Joe Burrow has 2,795 yards and 27 touchdown throws against six interceptions. Ja'Marr Chase has 64 catches for 878 yards and seven touchdowns. Chase Brown has 441 rushing yards. Boye Mafe has 6.5 sacks, and Barrett Carter has 74 tackles. Cincinnati has scored 278 points in nine games, and Laura can tell you where she was for most of them.

Laura: Twenty-seven touchdowns, Claire.

Claire: I heard you the first time. And the second.

Washington is 3-5-1 and has had a strange season. The Commanders lost three of their first four, played to a 27-27 tie with the Giants in October, and have since beaten the Eagles at home and won 24-21 in New York on Thursday night. They've had eleven days since, and Claire has used every one of them to convince herself this is a turning point.

Jayden Daniels has 1,499 yards and ten touchdown throws against two interceptions, plus 280 yards on the ground, and Claire says watching him is the closest thing football has to a great live album. Stefon Diggs has six touchdown catches. Odafe Oweh has five sacks, and Sonny Styles has 80 tackles.

Claire: We beat Seattle 33-31.

Laura: In September.

Claire: It still counts.

The album came out in 1976, went Diamond and won Album of the Year, and Claire has played it in her car on the way to every home game this season. "Sir Duke" for the drive in. "As" for the drive home, if things went well. She doesn't want to say what she plays if they didn't.

Laura: So you'll miss the show for a team that's 3-5-1.

Claire: I'll miss the show for my team. That's different.

Laura respects that, even if she won't say so. Cincinnati fans know a thing or two about loyalty to a team that hasn't always earned it.

They'll sit together in the lower bowl, and Claire will have the Stevie Wonder T-shirt she bought for the concert she isn't going to on beneath her coat, a small act of loyalty to both of the things she loves. Laura has promised to keep her voice down. Nobody who knows Laura believes her.

Somewhere downtown, around the third quarter, Stevie will play "I Wish," and Claire will feel it in her bones without hearing a note. She won't regret her choice. Probably. Laura will be too busy watching Chase to notice either way.

My call: Bengals 27, Commanders 23.
